title: Changing a Snowsports School Booking: Dates, Participants and Instructors
content:
Three kinds of change may be made to a Snowsports School booking once it is open: a move to another date, a re-registration to a different participant, and the assignment of the instructor who teaches it.

## 1. Moving a booking to another date

The following clause is **no longer in force**: "A booking may be moved to another date where the product allows it, up to the number of moves the product allows, and each move carries the product's move fee." It is carried here only so that no reader applies it, the current basis for what a change of date costs having replaced it.

A move to another date is accepted only when it is recorded on or before the move deadline, which is the product's notice period measured back from the moment the first session is due to start. The notice period is measured in whole elapsed hours on the mountain's local clock and is subtracted from the scheduled start of the first session to give the deadline; elapsed hours are never mixed with calendar days, and an hour begun is not an hour elapsed. The moment the first session is due to start is read from the booking record — the date the first session is due to run and the scheduled start on that date — matched by the booking reference. A move recorded at the deadline itself is on time.

A move does not reprice the booking: the tuition already raised stands even where the product costs more on the new date, and no difference is given back where it costs less.

## 2. Re-registering a booking to a different participant

A booking may be re-registered to a different participant where the product allows it and the new participant meets the product's age range and ability level, against the product's re-registration fee. The new participant's particulars are taken as the household states them, matched to the booking by its reference.

## 3. Instructors

Instructors are assigned by the school and may change up to the morning of the session. Where the household asked for a named instructor and the product allows the request, the request fee is raised and the collective makes good with credit if that instructor cannot teach the session after all.

## 4. Boundary readings of the move deadline

Take a booking of a product whose notice period is 72 hours, whose first session is due to start at 09:00 on a stated date. The deadline falls at 09:00 three days earlier.

| Moment the move is recorded | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| 08:59 on the deadline day | inside the notice period; the move is accepted |
| 09:00 on the deadline day | on the deadline; the move is accepted |
| 09:01 on the deadline day | the deadline has passed; the move is not accepted |

## 5. The three changes side by side

| Change | What the product must allow | What settles the condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| move to another date | that the product carries a move, within the moves it allows | the booking record and the product's notice period |
| re-registration | that the product carries a re-registration, and the new participant's age and level | the household's statement of the new participant, against the product's published range |
| named instructor | that the product carries a named-instructor request | the product's published terms |

The notice periods, move counts, move fees, re-registration availability and fees, minimum certification levels and named-instructor fees these terms turn on are published product by product on the Snowsports School tariff.
